nodes.name: An agent rarely does one thing. It reads, decides, acts,…
nodes.text: An agent rarely does one thing. It reads, decides, acts, looks at the result and decides again. Written down, most useful agent work follows a familiar shape: plan the change, make it, report what happened, and have someone review it.

nodes.name: The loop itself is not new. What is new is how fast it…
nodes.text: The loop itself is not new. What is new is how fast it runs and how little of it a person sees. A loop that runs unattended for an hour can do a lot of good work. It can also repeat a mistake many times, or act on a state of the world that changed halfway through. The design question is not whether agents should loop, but what keeps a loop honest.

nodes.name: Some steps should stop the loop and wait. Approving a…
nodes.text: Some steps should stop the loop and wait. Approving a change to shared guidance, publishing a page, granting access to a secret, installing a software update—these are decisions a person should make deliberately, with the details in front of them.

nodes.name: NullDull draws these lines in the product rather than in a…
nodes.text: NullDull draws these lines in the product rather than in a prompt. Agents can propose Memory changes, but approval of a member’s own proposal never comes from their agent. Agents can save Grid drafts, but Publish is a browser action for Grid managers. The CLI notices updates, but installing one needs your approval of the exact version and checksum. A connection can never approve changes, administer access or manage billing.

nodes.name: One of the most useful checkpoints is the gap between…
nodes.text: One of the most useful checkpoints is the gap between deciding what to do and doing it. Tasks, now in early access, is built around it. Every task has a mode. In **Plan** mode an agent reads the task, the repository and the relevant Memory files, writes its plan into the task, moves it to review and stops. Only when someone explicitly asks does the task switch to **Build**, where the agent claims it, reports progress at milestones and hands the result back for review.

nodes.name: Mode is separate from status, so “this needs a plan” and…
nodes.text: Mode is separate from status, so “this needs a plan” and “this is in progress” never get confused. Agents are told not to mark work done unless the user asks. The person who asked stays the person who decides.

nodes.name: Loops fail in the middle. A network call times out, a…
nodes.text: Loops fail in the middle. A network call times out, a session ends, a harness restarts. The dangerous moment is the retry: did the first attempt succeed? If the agent cannot tell, it might write twice.

nodes.name: NullDull operations carry request IDs and keep receipts.…
nodes.text: NullDull operations carry request IDs and keep receipts. Repeating a write with the same request ID returns the saved result instead of writing again. Model calls are not silently repeated after an ambiguous failure; an interrupted job is recorded and waits for an explicit retry. Writes also name the exact version they were based on, so a retry against a state that has since changed fails with a conflict instead of overwriting someone else’s work.

nodes.name: Loops need state outside the model.
nodes.text: ## Loops need state outside the model.

nodes.name: A loop that keeps its state only in the model’s context…
nodes.text: A loop that keeps its state only in the model’s context window cannot be inspected, resumed or shared. When the session ends, the plan ends with it. Durable state—a task with a plan and a status, a proposal waiting for review, a receipt for a write that already happened—lets a loop stop and start without losing its place, and lets a person see where it is.

nodes.name: That is why we think of shared memory and agent loops as…
nodes.text: That is why we think of shared memory and agent loops as one problem. The loop does the work; the state makes the work reviewable. A harness can poll for ready work on a schedule, but the server never pushes tasks into a local agent: the harness asks, within the permissions you granted, and reports back to a place your team can see.
